Three label-free candidates, each fused with L-SML and read out with the GAP rule: SUB5 (six telemetry channels), TELE16 (all 16 channels) and CHAIN16 (the PRM combined with the 16 channels). Development data; the Math-Shepherd PRM is excluded.

ProcessBench is the known limit. Its first-error metric is read out with the NC rule, which takes the gate (does the answer have an error at all) and the number of flagged steps from the PRM; the candidate only orders the steps. So ProcessBench numbers for "telemetry only" are not pure telemetry, and no telemetry-only rule is offered for it.

SUB5: six telemetry channels

  • What it does. Takes six token-level telemetry channels, z-scores each within its answer, groups them label-free into L-SML groups (at least three are required), weights the groups by L-SML (Dawid-Skene EM on per-answer GAP votes), and flags the top steps of each answer with the GAP count rule. Two variants: telemetry only (from the PRM's backbone or from the PRM's standalone base model), and SUB5 + PRM, where the PRM's step score enters as one more channel and anchors the weights.
  • What it measures. q15_H1 (spread of the top-15 next-token distribution), chosen_surprisal (how surprising the written token is), top15_turnover (how much the top-15 candidate set changes between tokens), dominant_freq16 (the dominant frequency of the uncertainty signal over a 16-token window), bocpd_p0 (Bayesian change-point probability) and digit_spread (spread of the probability over digit tokens).
  • Benchmarks. The six channels were chosen out of the 16 with PRMBench and Socratic labels, so those two are in sample; Hard2Verify, ProcessBench, CRV-Arith, CRV-GSM8K, PRM800K and DeltaBench are out of sample. Out of sample, telemetry only beats the PRM in — cells and its own plain average in —; SUB5 + PRM beats the PRM in — and its average in —.

TELE16: all 16 telemetry channels

  • What it does. The same pipeline on the full 16-channel bank: answer z-scores, label-free L-SML groups and weights, GAP readout. Telemetry only comes from the backbone or from the standalone base model. TELE16 + PRM (stored as PRMG_N16) puts the PRM's step score into that same L-SML as one more channel. It differs from CHAIN16, which first fuses the telemetry into group scores and only then combines them with the PRM.
  • What it measures. Uncertainty level: q15_H1, q15_VE1 (top-15 spread measures), chosen_surprisal, logprob_margin (gap between the two most likely tokens), energy_level, true_tail50 (mass outside the top 50). Change over the answer: energy_innovation, top15_turnover, top50_js (divergence between neighbouring top-50 distributions), bocpd_p0, realized_drv. Written token against the distribution: realized_z. Spectral: dominant_freq16. Digits: digit_alternative, digit_spread, digit_alternative_innovation.
  • Benchmarks. The 16-channel bank and the fusion recipe were developed on PRMBench, so PRMBench is in sample; Socratic was run afterwards as an external test and counts as out of sample here, as do the other six. Out of sample, telemetry only beats the PRM in — cells and its plain average (MEAN_N16) in —; TELE16 + PRM beats the PRM in — and its average (EQ_N16) in —.

CHAIN16: the PRM combined with the 16 channels

  • What it does. Two stages, both label-free: L-SML on the 16 channels gives one score per channel group; a second L-SML weighs the PRM's step score against those group scores; GAP flags the top steps (on ProcessBench, the PRM's own gate and count with CHAIN16's order). The telemetry can come from the backbone or from the standalone base model.
  • What it measures. The PRM's step score plus the same 16 telemetry channels as TELE16.
  • Benchmarks. Defined on PRMBench (in sample); every other benchmark is out of sample. Its plain-average control is EQ_N16, the equal-weight mean of the PRM and the 16 channels. Out of sample it beats the PRM in — cells and EQ_N16 in —.

Telemetry only vs PRISM, SLIDER and CROP

Each base model's own telemetry, with no PRM in the score, against the PRM built on that base model, under each competitor's own protocol and metrics. Every row is one pair: the standalone base model → its PRM. "TELE16" is L-SML over the 16 standalone channels, "Average" the same 16 channels with equal weights, "PRM" the paired PRM at its native threshold (reward ≤ 0.5 is an error). The competitor's published number is repeated on every row, with its paper and table. All values reproduce the stored PRM and TELE16 rows exactly (128 of 128 checks).

PRISM, Table 6: ProcessBench

Metric
Standalone model → paired PRMTELE16, telemetry ruleAverage, telemetry ruleTELE16, PRM gateAverage, PRM gatePRM, nativePublishedSystem and paperPublishedSystem and paper

TPR is accuracy on samples with an error (exact first-error step), TNR accuracy on error-free samples, F1 their harmonic mean. With the pure telemetry rule (first flagged step, Q80) average F1 is only —: it almost never answers "no error". The "PRM gate" columns use the PRM's native gate and error count with the arm's order, so they are not telemetry only. PRISM prints Omni-MATH and OlympiadBench cells that do not fit F1 as a harmonic mean; they are shown as printed, and its published average is our arithmetic over its four F1 cells.

SLIDER / Step-RRI: PRMBench redundancy class

Metric
Standalone model → paired PRMTELE16AveragePRM, nativePRM, same rule as TELE16PublishedSystem and paper

SLIDER publishes no code, so this comparison is approximate. It reports one "accuracy" read from a chart, with a threshold from a linear classifier on held-out labels; split, weighting and step-1 handling are not stated. We read their metric through their cosine baseline: on our split (10 problem-level 50/50 splits, a one-feature logistic-regression threshold) cosine gets —% against their —%, which points to plain accuracy with a class-balanced threshold. About 87% of steps are not redundant: always answering "not redundant" scores —% plain accuracy, so balanced accuracy is the fairer reading. SLIDER reports no balanced accuracy. In sample for TELE16.

CROP, Table 6: conformal clean prefix at α = 0.05

Standalone model → paired PRMTELE16AveragePRM, CROP's gridPRM, same grid as TELE16PublishedSystem and paperPublishedSystem and paperPublishedSystem and paper

Kept is the mean retained-prefix fraction, risk the share of test traces whose kept prefix holds an error (target ≤ 5%), AUROC pooled over test steps. 10 splits 60/20/20. CROP calibrates every threshold with labels and trains its LR rows on 60% of each set; our arms use no training split. The grids differ: CROP uses a fixed 101-point grid on its external sets, our arms a 201-quantile grid, so the PRM is shown on both. PRMBench is in sample for TELE16; our PRMBench uses all 6,211 answers (CROP sampled 5,000), and CROP used 20 splits on CRV.

The threshold is calibrated on one CRV set and applied to the other, so exchangeability is broken on purpose; CROP shows this as a failure diagnostic, and its table does not name the proxy. False acceptance and accepted traces follow our reading of its column names.

Not computed (they need new generation): PRISM's Best-of-N, guided decoding and GRPO tests, and CROP's repair accuracy. CROP's Math-Shepherd set is left out with its PRM.

"Beats average, PRM and best published" keeps a cell only when the candidate is above all three at once: its own plain average, the PRM itself under the same rule, and the best published score of any kind for that benchmark and metric. Cells with no published score never pass this filter.

Main metrics: PRMBench PRMScore; Socratic, CRV-Arith, CRV-GSM8K, PRM800K and DeltaBench step macro-F1; Hard2Verify official step balanced F1 (177 answers); ProcessBench average first-error F1. Every candidate and control uses the label-free GAP count rule; on ProcessBench the NC rule (the PRM's native gate and count, the arm's order). "The PRM itself" is that PRM under the same rule (ProcessBench: its native threshold).

Papers: PRMBench (arXiv 2501.03124, Table 3), PRISM (2606.09078), PathFinder-PRM (2505.19706), R-PRM (2503.21295), ActPRM (2504.10559), Socratic-PRMBench (2505.23474, Tables 3-4), Hard2Verify (2510.13744, Table 2), the Qwen PRM paper "The Lessons of Developing PRMs" (2501.07301, Table 7) for ProcessBench, and CROP (2605.30085, Table 6) for kept % and AUROC (its Direct PRM and Trace+PRM use Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B, so they are compared with that PRM only). PRM-specific published rows count only against the same PRM. Label-free published rows: uPRM and its LLM-as-a-Judge control (arXiv 2605.10158, Section 5.1; averages of the printed subset F1s are our arithmetic), ScalePRM (2512.03244; trained on LLM-generated verdicts, no ground truth), and ARES on PRMBench (2507.12948, Table 1; approximate: unstated subset, threshold tuned by 5-fold CV on labels, many LLM calls). DeltaBench has no published number on our metric. LLM critics and CROP's supervised rows use labels or many model calls that the candidates do not.

Two cells have no SUB5 score because the six channels form fewer than three L-SML groups: CRV-Arith backbone Qwen-72B (SUB5 + PRM) and CRV-Arith standalone Qwen-7B (SUB5 alone).
